questions.text: Other people's small hardships often matter to me too.
I experience guilt as a heavy, nauseating weight that settles in my gut and stays.
I routinely set ambitious goals for myself and dedicate significant effort to reaching them.
I prefer to let others take credit even when I did most of the work.
When a friend is hurting, my wish to help is often weaker than I expect it to be.
When someone tells me about a painful loss, I want to comfort them.
I schedule things back-to-back and adjust on the fly if something runs over.
I feel little concern when I hear that someone has been badly hurt.
I notice when a person clenches or unclenches their hands in rhythm with the emotional intensity of a conversation.
I use a decision journal to record significant choices and revisit them later.
I tend not to register the social dynamics of who gets the last word in a conversation.
I am attuned to the silent negotiations that happen before a group makes a decision.
I do not usually notice when a person glances at their companion for confirmation before committing to a plan.
I prefer that new team members be selected by the whole team together.
I feel compelled to act when I see inefficiency or lack of direction.
I notice when someone repeats a phrase another person used earlier to build rapport or to mock them.
I experience the sensation of calm not as something I achieve but as something I simply inhabit.
I gauge my productivity by how energized I feel, not by a tally of completed items.
Once a hard moment for someone has passed, I rarely give their wellbeing another thought.
I rarely miss a deadline because I build buffer time into my schedules.
I find it natural to sit back and let the group work through its process.
I find that eating alone at my favorite restaurant is a perfectly worthwhile way to spend an evening.
I update my to-do list throughout the day as new tasks surface.
I experience the ups and downs of life as gentle undulations rather than dramatic swings.
I rarely experience the physiological markers of stress even in stressful situations.
I enjoy the sense of being indispensable to a project's direction.
I share my perspective and then genuinely let the group weigh all viewpoints equally.
Even reading about an intense event can produce a strong physical reaction in me.
I am the kind of person who can be brought to tears by a commercial.
I feel that it is healthy and right to put my own needs first in most situations.
I do not usually pick up on whether someone is genuinely enthusiastic or just being polite.
I would happily take a pay cut if it meant funding a cause I care about.
I trust my gut instincts more than any amount of advance preparation.
I find myself correcting course when I think a group is going the wrong way.
I routinely reduce my own workload expectations so I can pitch in where others are struggling.
Knowing that people are still suffering keeps their wellbeing important to me after public attention has moved on.
